question: BBB profile discovery without on-site search: parse the robots-allowed BBB sitemaps (sitemap-business-profiles-index.xml lists 580 files) for profile slugs matching the legal names of the FY2024 top-15 sponsors and five processors (e.g. Fidelity Investments Charitable Gift Fund, Donor Advised Charitable Giving, Vanguard Charitable Endowment Program, American Online Giving Foundation, PayPal Charitable Giving Fund, Blackbaud Giving Fund, Dechomai), then read each profile's /complaints page and code giving-related items with the corpus scheme
conclusion_affected: Whether 'no BBB profile' for 18 of 20 entities is real or a discovery artefact; per-account BBB complaint rates
rationale: BBB on-site search is disallowed by robots.txt ('Disallow: /*?'), so this pass found profiles only through a search engine (Bonterra Tech, Blackbaud Inc). Absence is therefore 'not found', not 'none'. Sitemaps are explicitly allowed and would settle it

question: Grant-count denominators: collect FY2024 (or CY2024) grant counts, not dollars, from sponsors' own giving reports and press releases for the top-15 sponsors and the five processors (Fidelity Charitable reports 'nearly 2.7 million grants in 2024'); recompute complaint rates per 10,000 grants with Poisson intervals
conclusion_affected: Choice of denominator: per account vs per grant vs per $ grant; the Fidelity-vs-processor ranking flips between accounts and dollars
rationale: Rates per $1bn of grants and per 10,000 accounts rank AOGF/Benevity and Fidelity Charitable in opposite order (AOGF 28.7 vs Fidelity 2.1 per $bn; 0.78 vs 1.32 per 10k accounts, review venues). A grant-count denominator is the natural unit for delay complaints but the repo holds it for Fidelity only

question: What does DAFRC 'number_of_daf_accounts' measure at donation processors? Reconcile FY2024 values for AOGF (720,545, IRS 990), PayPal Charitable Giving Fund (380,644 filed), Givinga (1,421,011 paper), Blackbaud Giving Fund (460 imputed) and Network for Good/For Good (1 imputed) with each 990's Schedule D Part I line 1 and the processors' own descriptions (donor accounts, employer programs, or charity-designated funds)
conclusion_affected: Per-account complaint rates for processors; processor share of DAF accounts in market totals
rationale: Two of five processor account counts are imputed and one is implausible (1 account against $200m of grants), so per-account complaint rates cannot be computed for Network for Good and are unreliable for Blackbaud Giving Fund. The same field drives account-share figures elsewhere

question: Processor disbursement rules from public help centres: document payout thresholds, cadence and undeliverable-gift rules at Benevity/AOGF (paper-check minimum, monthly vs deferred payouts, 180-day void), YourCause/Blackbaud Giving Fund (registration-before-reissue and redirection to an employer-chosen charity) and Network for Good/For Good (holds pending compliance or tax issues); compare with sponsor-grant-payment-policies.csv
conclusion_affected: Synthesis E (nonprofit identity data leads complaints); whether processor delay complaints are policy (structural) or operations (fixable)
rationale: Grant delay is now the largest category in the 2021+ corpus (33 of 169 complaint/mixed records) and 21 of the 50 nonprofit records; most new items describe processor rules (a $75 gift held about eight months below a check threshold; a returned check redirected to another charity) rather than sponsor discretion

question: Alaska charity-page lawsuit (March 2026, Case No. 3AN-26-CI): identify all named defendants and the docket status from public court records or AG releases; confirm that PayPal Charitable Giving Fund and For Good (formerly Network for Good) are defendants, as BBB Wise Giving Alliance reports state
conclusion_affected: daf-litigation-2021plus.csv coverage; regulator complaints against processors
rationale: give.org reports (July and August 2026) name PPGF and For Good in the Alaska suit; the corpus (CMP-232) records the suit only as 'six platforms incl. GoFundMe and PayPal'

question: Venue-participation calibration: record each sponsor or processor app's public rating count and review count on the App Store and on Google Play's details page monthly (Fidelity Charitable Android: 29 reviews, 5K+ downloads; Benevity Android: 94 reviews, 50K+), to estimate reviews per active user and so scale review-venue complaint rates
conclusion_affected: Interpretation of every review-venue rate (reviewer share of users is unknown and differs by brand)
rationale: Google Play full review lists are robots-blocked (/store/getreviews and /_ batch endpoints), so only about three reviews per app are visible; the public counters are allowed and give the only venue-side denominator available
